primary_claim: Extending Anthropic's toy model of superposition to 26 additional activation functions shows loss is not meaningfully different across activation functions, degree of superposition is not correlated with loss beyond a certain threshold, and small variations in activation function shape (e.g. CELU vs. GELU) cause massive differences in superposition without corresponding differences in the loss landscape.

effect.metric: reconstruction loss range across activation functions

contradicts_or_qualifies: (Hard)sigmoid's enormous, quick superposition for unimportant features somewhat contradicts other research (project #3) which showed sigmoid incapable of developing superposition in other models
stated_future_work: more research needed on the weird behaviour of Sigmoid
more research needed on Exp/Exp(Linear) behavior which failed to converge for low sparsities
more research needed on SoLU's weird behavior
more research needed on Softplus's powerful, feature-indiscriminate superposition
limitations_stated: small exploration without previously formulated hypotheses or expectations, done merely to check for anything interesting in low-hanging fruit
(Hard)sigmoid's strange pattern may be a bug/floating point error
results are low-stakes and likely correct but not major insights
no LayerNorm or other modifications were applied to the initial networks
quote: Small variations in activation functions lead to massive differences in superposition (see CELU vs. GELU), which do not however translate into differences in the loss landscape.
